The correct sentence is: He couldn't help but feel a pang of regret as he gazed at the faded photograph, a visual reminder of the friendships he had let drift away over the years.

The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Under no circumstances / we can compromise on the / quality and safety of our products.
options_en: quality and safety of our products
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "we can compromise on the". When a sentence begins with a negative adverbial phrase like 'Under no circumstances', 'No sooner', 'Hardly', 'Seldom', etc., it requires inversion. This means the auxiliary verb must come before the subject. In this sentence, the auxiliary (modal) verb is 'can' and the subject is 'we'.

The correct structure is to place the auxiliary verb 'can' before the subject 'we'.

Correct Sentence: Under no circumstances can we compromise on the quality and safety of our products.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Amidst the bustling city, their laughter echoed like it had in the orphanage's hallways. Populism is a political strategy that prioritizes the concerns and interests of the general populace over those of the elite. Its emergence is characterized by increased backing for leaders or movements pledging to advocate for the grievances of ordinary citizens. Populist leaders frequently employ rhetoric that resonates with disenfranchised individuals, harnessing their dissatisfaction to gain support. Critics argue that populist movements often oversimplify intricate issues, promote divisive narratives, and weaken the essential checks and balances of democratic governance. questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['were' and 'was' respectively] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option b): The chef baked the cookies for the charity event. The participants provided the feedback after the workshop.

Select the idiom that can substitute the underlined group of words.

After years of hard work, she finally achieved her goal.
questions.solution_en:
Crossed the bridge: This means to deal with a problem when it arises.

Hit the sack: This means to go to bed or go to sleep.

Saw eye to eye: This means to agree with someone.

Hit the jackpot: This means to achieve great success or get exactly what you want, often unexpectedly or after hard work.

Given this analysis, the idiom "hit the jackpot" is the most suitable substitute for the underlined group of words, as it accurately describes achieving a goal after years of hard work. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The teacher looks after the students during the school trip. The students smile at the beautiful scenery they encounter.
options_en: The students are looked after by the teacher during the school trip. The beautiful scenery they encounter is smiled at by the students.
The students were looked after by the teacher during the school trip. The beautiful scenery they encounter was smiled at by the students.

questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verbs ['are' and 'is'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

In such questions, the preposition is kept intact with the verb while transforming the sentence into Passive Voice.

The Passive form of the sentence is: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + 'to be' + V3 + Preposition + by + Object.

Some verbs that have their prepositions intact in Passive voice: Look at, look down upon, look after, laugh at, smile at, enquired into, ignorant of.

Also, the sentence is in the Present Indefinite tense in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Present indefinite tense should be used.

For example:

The detective enquires into the case. (Active)

The case is enquired into by the detective.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option a): The students are looked after by the teacher during the school trip. The beautiful scenery they encounter is smiled at by the students.
